clue.text: For police state, dispatch riot formation

indicators.note: a formation is something arranged or formed anew, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heavy-handed order to send in officers to break up a riot in a repressive state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formation' tells you to rearrange DISPATCH RIOT; 'For' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime run through a police force's control over citizens is an autocracy ruled by one dictator.

clue.text: Ruin kept up by gallery

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for kept is read from bottom to top

parts.note: kept means saved
the Tate is the famous London art gallery

explanation.surface: A ruined artwork is propped up by a gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SAVED into DEVAS in this down clue; 'by' means next to. THE TATE is a group of art galleries in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To devastate is to wreck utterly, the verb sense of ruin.

clue.text: Shape coming from grotto around end of December

indicators.note: around means the cave word is placed around the letter that follows it

parts.note: a grotto is a cave

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of December

explanation.surface: A Christmas grotto taking shape at the end of December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' gives R from December; 'around' puts CAVE around it. 'coming from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To carve is to shape something by cutting, as with wood or stone.

clue.text: Puff with energy before exercise is practised

indicators.note: before places the energy letter ahead of the exercise abbreviation in the answer

parts.note: a puff is a promotional piece, an advert, shortened to AD
E is the physics symbol for energy
PT is physical training, i.e. exercise

explanation.surface: Smoking with vigour before a workout makes you an old hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puff' suggests breathing or smoking, but here it is a promotional puff, an AD. 'with' and 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone adept is skilled through experience, which is what practised means as an adjective.

clue.text: Get up too sharply?

parts.note: get up means to dress oneself; doing it too sharply means wearing clothes too smart for the occasion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Get up' looks like rising quickly from bed, but a get-up is an outfit and 'sharply' means smartly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressing more formally or showily than an occasion needs is to be too sharply turned out.

clue.text: He visits places, say, always ancient

indicators.note: say signals that the word for places is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: places are sites, which sounds like sights
e'er is the old, poetic form of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A traveller who, as it were, always tours ancient places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives SIGHTS, a sound-alike of SITES (places); 'ancient' marks E'ER as an archaic way of writing ever.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist goes round to look at notable places, so he is a visitor.

clue.text: First bars of cast iron holding temperature

indicators.note: holding means the reshaped letters enclose the temperature abbreviation
metal that is cast is poured into a new shape, so the letters of iron are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cast iron kept at a certain heat, like the opening of a foundry piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' rearranges IRON to INRO; 'holding' puts T inside, after the N.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction to a song is its opening few bars of music.

clue.text: Quack heard in the sky?

parts.note: a quack is slang for a medic; one working from the air, as in the Australian outback service

explanation.walkthrough: 'Quack' suggests a duck overhead, but it is slang for a doctor, here one who travels by plane to remote patients.
explanation.definitionFit: A medic who reaches remote patients by aircraft, famous in the Australian outback, is a doctor airborne.

clue.text: Stagger back carrying volume in bar

indicators.note: carrying means the reversed word holds the volume letter inside
back means the word for stagger is read in reverse

parts.note: to stagger is to reel

explanation.surface: Someone stumbling out of a pub with a large drink in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns REEL into LEER; 'carrying' puts V inside it. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lever is a rigid rod used to prise or lift, a kind of bar.

clue.text: Greet with nice fresh bubbly

indicators.note: fresh suggests something made new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A welcome offered with a glass of good champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges GREET and NICE together. 'bubbly' looks like champagne but is the definition, meaning lively.
explanation.definitionFit: A bubbly person is full of lively vigour, which is what energetic describes.

clue.text: Cent remains next to note in here

definitions.text: Cent remains next to note in here

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning
to note something is to register it

explanation.surface: A coin lies among ashes beside a banknote in a till drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'next to' places the pieces side by side. The whole clue also describes the till, where coins and notes are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop till holds the coins and banknotes taken from customers, so money is kept in it.

clue.text: Studied bookworm, say, holding page by journalist

indicators.note: holding means the creature word encloses the page abbreviation

parts.note: a bookworm is literally a small grub, an example of an insect
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: An avid reader pored over a page written by a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bookworm' suggests a keen reader, but 'say' shows it is an example: the insect that eats books. 'by' is a link meaning next to.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something closely is to have looked it over carefully, the past tense of scrutinise.

clue.text: Left-wingers wrong returning socialist leader

indicators.note: returning means the legal word for a wrong is read backwards

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of socialist

explanation.surface: Radicals return after a socialist chief is wronged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns TORT into TROT; 'leader' gives S. Trots is slang for Trotskyists.
explanation.definitionFit: Trots is informal for followers of Trotsky, a group of radical socialists.

clue.text: Appreciation of Greek school of thought, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals the words are spoken, so the spelling can differ

parts.note: GR is short for Greek, and an attitude is a way of thinking, a school of thought

explanation.surface: Admiring a philosophy from ancient Athens, as people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' means GR plus ATTITUDE, said quickly, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Thankfulness for a kindness is appreciation of it.

clue.text: Pickled with brine I eat nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone eating a gherkin, fresh from the brine, claims to have gone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' rearranges BRINE I EAT. 'Pickled' suggests the brine but means drunk. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pickled is slang for drunk, and inebriate as an adjective means intoxicated.

clue.text: Stress is less taking train, perhaps

indicators.note: taking puts the railway word straight after the word for less

parts.note: under means less than, below
a train runs on a railway line, so the word suggests it by association

explanation.surface: Commuting by train is said to be less stressful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'train, perhaps' points to a railway LINE. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To emphasise a point is to stress it, as if marking it with a ruled stroke beneath.

clue.text: English bishop has zero resistance for sin

parts.note: RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
O looks like zero
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: An English bishop with no resistance to temptation commits a sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' and 'for' are links. RR stands for Right Reverend, the formal style of a Church of England bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A sin is a moral wrong, a mistake in conduct.

clue.text: Bank's backing electronic payment? Say again

indicators.note: backing means the word for a bank or row is reversed, read upward in this down clue

parts.note: a bank, as of seats, is a tier
E is short for electronic, as in e-mail
a rate is a payment, as in a fee charged

explanation.surface: Is a bank supporting electronic payment? Ask once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns TIER into REIT. 'Bank' suggests money, but here it is a row, a tier.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat oneself is to say something over again.

clue.text: Big in Tokyo? Be serious!

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the run of words Tokyo be serious

explanation.surface: Sumo wrestlers are big in Japan, someone insists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' hides the answer across TOKYO BE SERIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means very fat, so extremely big in body.

clue.text: Renouncing weapons and winning

definitions.meaning: giving up arms, as a country laying down its forces
winning in the sense of charming, engaging

explanation.surface: A side laying down arms yet still coming out on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winning' looks like victory but means charming; 'and' joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking away weapons is the literal sense; an engaging, charming smile is the figurative one.

clue.text: Tall object which enclosed rapunzel initially

definitions.text: Tall object which enclosed rapunzel initially

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the five preceding words

explanation.surface: The fairy-tale structure that imprisoned Rapunzel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of the five words; the whole clue also describes where Rapunzel was kept.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fairy tale, Rapunzel is locked in a high stone structure, a turret.

clue.text: Start of wrinkles — bad sign, possibly, for them

definitions.text: Start of wrinkles — bad sign, possibly, for them

indicators.note: start of means the opening letter of wrinkles

parts.note: an omen is a sign, and possibly a bad one

explanation.surface: The first wrinkle seen as a bad sign by certain people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start of' gives W, followed by OMEN; the whole clue suggests those who dread the first wrinkle.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue paints a stereotype of ladies worried about ageing, so the whole clue points to them.

clue.text: Blasted slugs coming back!

parts.note: slugs are bullets; fired ones bouncing back off a surface towards the shooter

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blasted slugs' looks like a gardener cursing pests, but slugs are bullets that have been fired.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullets that rebound off a hard surface are said to deflect back, the verb for a rebound.

clue.text: About time head of state shuts up

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
an age is a period of time

indicators.note: head of picks the opening letter of state

explanation.surface: A sovereign closes debate after some time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shuts up' suggests silencing, but here means confining. 'head of' gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: To confine an animal behind bars is to shut it up.

clue.text: Conservative member's ascent

parts.note: C is short for Conservative, the British political party
a member is a limb of the body

explanation.surface: A Tory MP's rise up the political ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' suggests a party member but means an arm or leg. 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb is an upward journey, the act of ascending.

clue.text: Mad about a politician going berserk

indicators.note: about means the word for mad goes around the next two pieces

parts.note: raging means mad, furious
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An angry politician losing control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A and MP inside RAGING.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampaging means running wild violently, so behaving in a frenzy.

clue.text: Independent magazine with eye-opening picture

indicators.note: opening means the first letter of eye

explanation.surface: A magazine publishing a striking photograph that opens the eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eye-opening' looks like a single adjective, but 'opening' gives the first letter of 'eye', E. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture, as a likeness or photograph.

clue.text: Specious beliefs end in disaster

indicators.note: disaster suggests ruin, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Misguided convictions eventually come to grief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disaster' rearranges BELIEFS END IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A specious argument only looks plausible and cannot really be justified.
